name: Self-Injurious Behavior
summary: Actions that cause harm to oneself — head-banging, hand-biting, excessive scratching — which can stem from communication difficulty, sensory needs, pain, or emotional overwhelm and warrants prompt professional assessment.
triggers: Inability to communicate pain, discomfort, or an unmet need
Escape or avoidance of an overwhelming task or environment
Sensory-seeking (craving intense proprioceptive or tactile input)
Underlying pain or medical issue (e.g. headache, GI discomfort, ear infection)
Extreme frustration or emotional distress with no other outlet

remedies.text: Rule out pain or a medical cause first — self-injury can be the only way a nonverbal or minimally verbal child signals physical distress
Functional behavior assessment with a BCBA or psychologist to determine the behavior's function before intervening
Teach and reinforce an alternative way to get the same need met (communication device, requesting a break, requesting sensory input safely)
Protective equipment (padded mitts, helmets) as a short-term safety measure while the underlying cause is addressed, not as a standalone fix
